title: Shared definitions of the flagplot-agent answers, version 1

dec.description: A fixed-point quantity as an exact decimal string, such as "12" or "0.25". Never a float.

handle.description: A unit named by kind and number as the log names it, with its name when the side knows one (its own units only).

place.description: A hex, its latitude and longitude where the map has them, and the name of the side's own base there.

event_numbers.description: The side's own numbers of events (1, 2, 3 in the order its view gives them), as explain takes them. The log's numbers never appear.

land_unit_line.description: A land unit of the side (decision 0066, 21): its men ashore and where, its men aboard by ship, and whether its men were fed in the last night pulse. Only the side's own units have one.

destroyed.description: No man left, ashore or aboard. The unit keeps its number.

fed_last_night.description: How the side's men ashore in the unit's hex were fed in the last night pulse, from the side's own MenFed event: fed, partly_fed or unfed. not_ashore for a unit with no man ashore; not_known when the side holds no such event for the hex.

fatigue.description: How tired the unit is, 0 to 100 (decision 0090, 11). It cuts the men who fire and nothing else.

fed_share.description: The share of the unit's men fed at the last night's charge, 0 to 1 (decision 0090, 8): 1 until the first night and for a unit with no man ashore at the charge.

posture_order.description: The number of the side's standing posture order, when one is in force. Left out otherwise.

march.description: The unit's march, when a march order is standing (decision 0094, 4 and 11). The unit is where it was until it has marched all the days. Left out when it has none.

days_marched.description: The days marched so far, below of_days.

days_counted.description: The days counted toward of_days (decision 0098, 4): each day marched counts as the unit's movement factor for the hexes it leaves and enters. Equal to days_marched for a unit of standard movement.

of_days.description: The days a march takes: the scenario's march_days_per_hex.

order.description: The number of the side's march order, when it is still known.

falling_back.description: Set when the march is a falling back after a defeat (decision 0104), which has no order: the hex of the defeat and the event that records it. The unit carries no supply.

march_to.description: The hexes the unit's men ashore can be ordered to march to: the neighbours the map joins to their hex by a land link, in hex order (decision 0094, 1 and 3). Left out when there are none: on a map with no land links, and for a unit with no man ashore.

activity.description: What the unit does on a day it does not march or fight (decisions 4 of 0099 and 4 of 0097): ready (rehearses a landing when it is on a roster; the default), train or work (at the job below).

working.description: True for a working unit (decision 0099): it only works, is always on defend, never attacks, and its men do not fire or hold a base. Left out when false.

job.description: The job a unit set to work makes its work at: the one its order names, else the default (the airfield of its base if it has none, else the port). Left out when the unit does not work.

job_is_default.description: True when job is the default one because no job was named. Left out when false.

activity_order.description: The number of the side's set_activity order, when one is in force. Left out otherwise.

experience.description: The unit's experience, 0 to 4 (decision 0097, 1): 2 is its service's standard. It moves its chance to hit.

skills.description: What the unit is good at (decision 0098): each 0 to 4, 2 the standard, fixed in play. Shown for the side's own units only.

assault.description: Assault from the sea: moves the rehearsal gained a day.

holding.description: Holding ground: moves the chance to hit while its side defends.

weight.description: Weight: moves its shots and each man's daily supply.

works.description: Works: moves the work the unit makes a day, as the skill over 2 (decision 0099, 2).

movement.description: Movement by the terrain of the hex; a march uses the lower skill of the hex left and the hex entered.

training.description: Days of training counted toward the next step of experience (decision 0097, 3).

of_days.description: The days a step takes: the scenario's training_days_per_level.

up_to.description: The experience training raises a unit to and no further: the scenario's training_ceiling.

fighting.description: Days of firing in a fight counted toward the next step of experience (decision 0097, 5).

of_days.description: The days a step takes: the scenario's fight_days_per_level.

rehearsal.description: The unit's rehearsal of a landing (decision 0095, 3), while it has one. Left out when it has none.

hex.description: The hex the rehearsal is for.

roster.description: The roster of a force the unit is on (decision 0095, 1). Left out when it is on none.

hex.description: The hex of the force's prepare_landing order.

landing_fatigue.description: The fatigue the unit would gain when its first men land at that hex, from its rehearsal for it (decision 0095, 6): the engine's own function.

movement.description: A force steams at the speed of its slowest ship. cannot_move: a ship afloat has propulsion out, so the force has no speed whatever its status and route say. slowed: a ship has propulsion degraded. normal: neither.

cargo_supply_t.description: Tons of supply carried as cargo, summed over the ships afloat. null unless the force carries some supply or fuel cargo or its mission is transport.

cargo_fuel_t.description: Tons of fuel carried as cargo (not the fuel the ships burn), summed over the ships afloat. null under the same condition.

act_at.description: Decision 0096: the waypoints of the force's route it is marked to act at that it has not passed (a halted force's own hex included while it lies there), in hex order; never the last waypoint. Left out when none.

halt.description: Decision 0096: present while the force is halted at a marked waypoint (status halted). Left out otherwise.

since.description: The clock time it halted, such as D1 22:00.

waits_for.description: What it waits to do before it steams on: bombard (done in a night pulse), cargo, or both in that order.

bombarded.description: true once it has bombarded since it halted; left out until then.

preparation.description: Decision 0095: the landing the force is prepared for, by a prepare_landing order. Left out when it has none.

hex.description: The coast hex the landing is for.

roster.description: The land units that are to land from the force, in number order.

loading.description: The force's loading for that hex, 0 to 100.

landing_rate.description: The share of the port's rate the force would unload at in hex, men and cargo alike (decision 0095, 5): the engine's own landing_rate_factor. 1 is the port's rate.

order.description: The number of the side's prepare_landing order, when it is still known.

landing_at.description: Decision 0095, 5: the hex where the force has begun landing men and its unloading is not yet complete; until it is, it works at the rate of a landing there. Left out when it is not landing.

propulsion_lines.description: The ships afloat whose propulsion is not working, each with its state.

location.description: The base or the ship the group is at; null for a group lost with a base that changed side (decision 0090, 20), which has no place.

lost_with_base.description: True only for a group lost with a base that changed side. Left out otherwise.

pilots.description: Pilots of the group. null means the scenario does not count this group's pilots (decision 0038): no pilot limit applies and every ready aircraft can fly. A number means the group can fly no more aircraft than it has pilots.

strike_radius_nm.description: The aircraft type's strike radius in miles: how far from the group's place a strike can be flown (for a fighter, the radius within which its escorts go with a raid). "0" for a type that cannot strike.

search_range_nm.description: The aircraft type's search range in miles: the furthest a search arc can reach. "0" for a type that cannot search.

reach_nm.description: Given only for a group on extended reach (set_reach): the reach in force in miles, more than strike_radius_nm. Left out on normal reach, where the reach is strike_radius_nm.

target_priority.description: Given only for a group whose target list is not the default (set_target_priority): the kinds of ship its strikes go for, in order. A contact of a kind not on the list is never launched at. Left out where the list is every kind in the order carrier, battleship, cruiser, destroyer, transport, auxiliary.

moved_yesterday.description: Given (true) only for a group that a rebase order moved to its present base on the day just resolved (decision 0091): it flew nothing on that day, and its aircraft were on the ground at this base. Left out otherwise.

kept_on_ground_by_field.description: Given only for a group at a base whose airfield is damaged (decision 4 of 0103), when the field keeps at least one of the group's crewed aircraft on the ground: how many, and the field's damage. The field lets 100 less the damage, over 100, of the group's crewed aircraft fly. Left out otherwise.

would_strike.description: Given only for a group on naval_strike with ready aircraft that would launch now: the contact the staff would send it at if the strike decision were made at this moment, by the rule the decision uses (a contact reported in this pulse or the one before, within the group's reach, of a kind on its target list; the kind first on the list, then the nearest). The decision is made in each daylight pulse on the contacts held then, so a contact that is not sighted again may be too old by the morning. Left out when the group would launch at nothing.

base_works.description: A base's airfield, work and defences (decision 0099), for the side's own bases only. Left out while the base has an airfield, none is being built, no defences are raised and no work of yesterday waits to be read.

airfield.description: Whether the base has an airfield. No group can rebase to or land at a base that has none.

airfield_work.description: The work done on the airfield so far.

airfield_work_needed.description: The work the airfield needs in all (the ground figure airfield_work). Left out once the base has an airfield.

defences.description: The base's defences, 0 to 100: while the side defends the hex its units' chance to hit rises with them.

port_work_yesterday.description: The work on the port made yesterday: what today's cargo at the base reads.

aircraft_work_yesterday.description: The work on the aircraft made yesterday: what tonight's repairs read.

airfield_damage.description: The damage to a base's airfield (decision 0103), for the side's own bases only. Left out while the damage is 0.

damage.description: The damage, above 0 and up to 100.

share_that_flies.description: How many of every 100 of a group's ready aircraft the field lets fly: 100 less the damage.

takes_aircraft.description: Whether a rebase to the field is accepted and aircraft land on it. False at or above refused_at, and a field with no airfield.

refused_at.description: The damage at or above which the field takes no aircraft (the ground figure airfield_landing_refused_at). Left out without the ground figures.

port_size.description: The map's port size of the hex, 0 where the map gives none. In the rules as built it sets only how fast cargo is worked: a port of size 0 has no berths and ships load and unload by lighter at that size's rate. Any ship may stop at a base of any size, and refuelling does not depend on it.

airfield_size.description: The map's airfield size of the hex, 0 where the map gives none. No rule reads it: a base of size 0 launches and receives air groups, repairs and is raided like any other, and no limit on the aircraft at a base follows from it.

ground_estimate_line.description: The side's estimate of the enemy's men ashore in one hex (decision 0092): the count of the last ground report there, which can be wrong by up to half either way, never aged and never corrected until a new report replaces it. day is the day it was reported (0 for an opening estimate) and age_days the days from then to the last day resolved. The true count and the error of the report are never given.

event.description: The side's number of the report; explain on it shows what the side may know of it.

taken_for.description: The kind of the most important ship the sighting reported. Like ship_count it is what was reported: it can be wrong, and can change when the contact is seen again.

not_known.description: The one answer for anything the side does not know of. It carries nothing of the question.

enemy_base_line.description: A base the side does not own, as every side knows it: number, name, place and the side that holds it. Nothing else is known of it.
